@title AMLSystem
 @dev Central admin contract for the AML demo system. Owns the global
      suspicious-amount threshold, maintains an independent blacklist
      registry, keeps a running transaction log, and exposes aggregate
      system statistics pulled from UserRegistry, FundRequest, and
      PaymentProcessor.
 NOTE: This contract maintains its OWN blacklist (`blacklist` /
 `blacklistReasons`), separate from UserRegistry's per-user
 `isBlacklisted` flag. The two are independent by design of the given
 spec — see the integration note at the bottom of this file for the
 implications of that split.
@notice Address administering this contract.
@notice Running counter used to assign unique transaction log IDs (1-indexed).

@notice Amount above which a logged transaction is auto-flagged as
         suspicious. Defaults to 5 ether.
@notice Maps transaction log ID to its full record.
@notice This contract's own blacklist, independent of UserRegistry's.
@notice Reason recorded for each blacklisted address.
@notice List of all addresses ever blacklisted through this contract.
@notice Reference to the deployed UserRegistry contract.
@notice Reference to the deployed FundRequest contract.
@notice Reference to the deployed PaymentProcessor contract.
@notice Emitted when admin control is transferred to a new address.

@title FundRequest
 @dev Handles the lifecycle of money requests created by users holding the
      REQUESTER role in UserRegistry, from creation through approval,
      rejection, completion, or cancellation.
 NOTE: This contract only manages request *state*. Actual value transfer
 is handled by a companion PaymentProcessor contract, which is linked via
 setPaymentProcessor() and is the only address authorized to call
 updateRequestAsApproved / updateRequestAsCompleted / updateRequestAsRejected.
@notice Running counter used to assign unique request IDs (1-indexed).
@notice Maps request ID to its full record.
@notice Maps a user address to the list of request IDs they created.
@notice List of request IDs currently in PENDING status.
@notice Reference to the deployed UserRegistry contract.

@dev Simple on-chain heuristic threshold used to auto-flag unusually
      large requests as suspicious. This is a placeholder signal only —
      a real AML system would rely on off-chain risk scoring rather
      than a single static amount threshold.
@notice Emitted when the admin links the PaymentProcessor contract.
@dev Restricts a function to addresses registered in UserRegistry.

@title PaymentProcessor
 @dev Handles FUNDER approval/rejection of fund requests and the actual
      ETH transfer from FUNDER to REQUESTER. Applies a simple on-chain
      AML amount threshold to flag large payments for review.
 Setup: after deploying UserRegistry, FundRequest, and this contract, the
 admin must call:
   - UserRegistry.setPaymentProcessorContract(address(this))
   - FundRequest.setPaymentProcessor(address(this))
 so this contract is authorized to update registry stats and request state.
 NOTE: The AML threshold here is a simple static amount check for
 demonstration purposes. A production AML system would use off-chain risk
 scoring, behavioral pattern analysis, and sanctions-list checks rather
 than a single fixed ETH amount, and would not gate compliance on the
 "wealth" of either party.
@notice Running counter used to assign unique payment IDs (1-indexed).

@notice Payments strictly above this amount (in wei) are flagged as
         suspicious for compliance review. Defaults to 5 ether.
@notice Maps payment ID to its full record.

@notice Maps a user address (funder or requester) to the payment IDs
         they were involved in.
@notice Reference to the deployed UserRegistry contract.
@notice Reference to the deployed FundRequest contract.
@notice Emitted when a FUNDER rejects a pending request.
@dev Restricts a function to addresses registered in UserRegistry.

documentation.text:
@title UserRegistry
 @dev Manages user registration, roles, and blacklist status for an
      Anti-Money Laundering (AML) demo system.
 Roles:
  - REQUESTER: a user who can request funds
  - FUNDER:    a user who can approve/send funds
  - ADMIN:     privileged role able to blacklist/whitelist users
 NOTE: This contract is intended as an educational / prototype building
 block. A production AML system would additionally need off-chain risk
 scoring, KYC integration, and should never gate compliance decisions on
 income level alone.
@notice Address that deployed the contract and administers the registry.
@notice Running count of all registered users.
@notice Maps a wallet address to its full User profile.
@notice Quick lookup of whether an address has ever registered.

@notice Address of the deployed FundRequest contract, authorized to
         increment request counters. Set once by admin after deployment.

@notice Address of the deployed PaymentProcessor contract, authorized
         to increment payment counters. Set once by admin after deployment.
@notice Emitted when a new user successfully registers.
@notice Emitted when an existing user updates their profile.
@notice Emitted when the admin blacklists a user.
@notice Emitted when the admin removes a user from the blacklist.
@notice Emitted when the admin links a companion contract.
